title: Pricing experimentation approval matrix and SQ gating for enterprise deals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We are running a set of pricing/packaging experiments aimed at increasing average contract value for enterprise customers while protecting unit economics. Several recent deals uncovered unclear approval boundaries for discounting tied to feature bundles, reserved capacity, and security/compliance concessions (e.g., extended data retention, on-prem deployment). Sales and Finance requested tighter guardrails and an integrated flow that prevents deals from moving forward without SQ (security questionnaire) and legal gating when certain pricing levers are used.

Objective: Define and operationalize an approval matrix that: (1) classifies experiments and ad-hoc discounts by risk and economic impact, (2) defines approvers and SLAs for each class, (3) embeds SQ routing into the deal intake flow so security/compliance artifacts are collected early, and (4) updates the pricebook and contract playbook to reflect experiment allowances.

Scope: This ticket covers the PM-side design of the matrix, SLAs, and SQ gating criteria plus coordination items for SalesOps, Legal, Finance, and Engineering (for Console/CRM changes). Implementation tasks (UI changes and automation) are owned by ENG-24201 and will be tracked as dependent tickets.

Proposal summary: 1) Create three experiment tiers: Tier A (low-risk, <15% list discount, no custom terms), Tier B (mid-risk, 15-35% discount, may include reserved capacity pricing or limited term changes), Tier C (high-risk, >35% discount or any bespoke security/compliance request such as on-prem, data residency, or KMS/HSM integration). 2) Approval routing: Tier A - Sales manager sign-off within 48h; Tier B - Sales manager + Finance within 72h; Tier C - Pricing Council (PM/Finance/Legal/Security) within 5 business days. 3) SQ gating: any Tier B or C deal must trigger an automated SQ intake form and create a Legal & Security review ticket before the contract signature milestone. 4) Emergency exception path for time-sensitive renewals: short-form exec sign-off plus post-hoc audit and mandatory follow-up remediation plan.

Decision points needed: - Confirm threshold percentages for discount bands and whether list price references should be net or gross. - Agree on final approver roles for Pricing Council and required quorum. - Determine whether certain security concessions (e.g., SOC report sharing) are Tier A or Tier B.

Success metrics: - 90% of Tier B/C deals have SQ intake completed before sending redlines. - 0 major revenue leakage incidents (contract disputes) attributable to unclear approval rules in next 6 months. - Time-to-approval median: Tier A <48h, Tier B <72h, Tier C <5 business days. - Pricing experiment results (ARPA uplift) measured against control cohorts for Q2.

Rollout plan: 1) Finalize matrix and runbook (PM owner) - due 2025-03-12. 2) Engineering implement automation hooks in Console and Salesforce (ENG-24201) - rollout in console-2025.03. 3) Legal/Security integrate SQ templates and acceptance criteria. 4) Sales Ops training and playbook update. 5) Pilot with top 5 AE teams for 4 weeks, iterate, then scale.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: Approval latency slows deal cycle. Mitigation: pre-qualification checklist and SLA dashboards in Console. - Risk: Sales bypassing process for urgent renewals. Mitigation: emergency exception audit with retroactive approvals and penalty for repeat bypass. - Risk: Misclassification of security concessions. Mitigation: explicit mapping spreadsheet and one-off advisory calls during pilot.

Stakeholders: Sales, SalesOps, Finance, Legal, Security, Platform Engineering, PMM.

Next steps: circulate this doc to PM/Finance/Legal/Security for sign-off, finalize thresholds, and hand off automation requirements to ENG-24201.
